content_voiceover: This summary table of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes is extremely high yield and often tested by matching clinical triad to gene to diagnostic test. Fanconi anemia presents with skin pigmentation changes, short stature, radial ray and thumb abnormalities, and craniofacial, genitourinary, gastrointestinal, or cardiac anomalies, plus aplastic anemia and a strong predisposition to AML and solid tumors like squamous cell carcinoma, brain tumors, and Wilms tumor. It's inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern through genes like FANCA, FANCC, and several others, with one X-linked gene, FANCB, and the diagnostic test is chromosome breakage studies using agents like diepoxybutane. Dyskeratosis congenita has the classic triad of abnormal nails, reticular skin pigmentation, and oral leukoplakia, with predisposition to marrow failure, malignancy, and pulmonary fibrosis. It can be X-linked recessive through DKC1, autosomal dominant through TERC, TERT, or TINF2, or autosomal recessive, and the diagnostic test is telomere length measurement, since these are telomerase complex defects. Shwachman-Diamond syndrome combines exocrine pancreatic insufficiency with bone marrow failure and skeletal anomalies, is autosomal recessive through SBDS, and is diagnosed with serum trypsinogen and pancreatic isoamylase levels. Finally, congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia presents in the neonatal period with bleeding and carries AML risk, is autosomal recessive through c-MPL, the thrombopoietin receptor gene, and shows a normal cellular marrow but absent megakaryocytes.
keypoints: Fanconi anemia: chromosome breakage test, AR (FANCA/C/etc), ↑AML/solid tumor risk
Dyskeratosis congenita: triad of nails/rash/leukoplakia, telomere length test
Shwachman-Diamond: exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, ↓trypsinogen/isoamylase, SBDS gene
CAMT: neonatal bleeding, absent megakaryocytes, c-MPL mutation
keypoint_voiceover: Match each syndrome to its test. Fanconi anemia is diagnosed with chromosome breakage studies and features radial ray anomalies plus high AML and solid tumor risk. Dyskeratosis congenita has the nails, reticular rash, and leukoplakia triad, diagnosed by telomere length. Shwachman-Diamond syndrome combines exocrine pancreatic insufficiency with marrow failure, confirmed by serum trypsinogen and pancreatic isoamylase. And congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia presents with neonatal bleeding, absent megakaryocytes on a normal cellular marrow, and a c-MPL mutation.
